records.title: Voretigene Neparvovec (Luxturna) for Biallelic RPE65-Associated Retinal Dystrophy: Systematic Review.

content.title: Voretigene Neparvovec (Luxturna) for Biallelic RPE65-Associated Retinal Dystrophy: Systematic Review.
content.abstract:
Topic

Biallelic RPE65-associated inherited retinal disorders (IRDs) cause progressive vision loss, impaired light sensitivity, and reduced mobility. Voretigene neparvovec-rzyl (LUXTURNA), the first FDA-approved gene therapy for this condition, is a disease-modifying option whose clinical benefits and harms warrant synthesis.

Clinical relevance

Patients with biallelic RPE65-associated IRDs often have severe functional impairment despite variable BCVA changes. Understanding treatment effects on BCVA, light sensitivity, VF, and adverse events is essential for referral timing, counseling, and monitoring.

Methods

Ovid MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from January 2000 through October 2025 for randomized trials and observational studies evaluating voretigene neparvovec-rzyl in RPE65-associated IRDs. The primary outcome was BCVA; secondary outcomes included full-field stimulus threshold (FST), visual field (VF), and adverse events including chorioretinal atrophy and central retinal thickness (CRT) change. Findings were synthesized narratively for the systematic review, with random-effects meta-analyses for perifoveal atrophy incidence and CRT change where data allowed.

Results

Twenty-eight studies met inclusion criteria, encompassing 376 individuals and 673 treated eyes. BCVA outcomes were variable and generally modest, with somewhat greater gains in pediatric than adult cohorts. Light sensitivity improved consistently on FST, evident by 1 month and sustained through 6 months in the largest cohort (mean change -18.24 dB); 1 study reported greater 12-month gains in children (13 dB) than adults (8 dB). VF improved substantially in the pivotal trial cohort (92% mean increase at 1 year, sustained to 3-4 years), with more equivocal findings in real-world pediatric cohorts. Chorioretinal atrophy and intraocular inflammation were the most frequently reported adverse events. Pooled analysis of 3 studies estimated 75% of treated eyes (95% CI, 57%-89%) developed new or progressive perifoveal atrophy; CRT changes ranged from a mean increase of 8.3 µm to a decrease of 27.5 µm. Severe complications such as retinal tears and detachment were infrequent.

Conclusion

Voretigene neparvovec-rzyl is associated with improvements in light sensitivity and VF in pediatric patients treated before advanced degeneration, while BCVA gains are variable and usually modest. Chorioretinal atrophy, including perifoveal atrophy in a majority of treated eyes, is a common structural finding warranting monitoring alongside functional benefits.

records.title: Image-Based Artificial Intelligence for Automated Diagnosis and Clinical Activity Grading in Thyroid Eye Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

content.title: Image-Based Artificial Intelligence for Automated Diagnosis and Clinical Activity Grading in Thyroid Eye Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Topic

To evaluate image-based artificial intelligence (AI) accuracy for thyroid eye disease (TED) diagnosis and clinical activity grading (Clinical Activity Score [CAS] ≥ 3 vs. <3) and compare AI with ophthalmologists.

Clinical relevance

TED diagnosis and activity grading are challenging because of overlapping signs and subjective CAS (interrater variability up to 30%). Its consolidated accuracy is unquantified.

Methods

We searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library through November 13, 2025, for studies of TED diagnosis or activity grading using image-based AI. Risk of bias was assessed with PROBAST+AI and certainty with Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE). Bivariate random-effects models pooled sensitivity, specificity, and area under the curve (AUC).

Results

Nineteen studies (n = 8744) were included: 8 evaluated diagnosis (11 validation sets; n = 4662) and 11 activity grading (11 validation sets; n = 4082). For diagnosis, sensitivity was 0.93 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.86-0.96), specificity 0.84 (95% CI, 0.78-0.88), and AUC 0.93 (95% CI, 0.90-0.95); after outlier exclusion, 0.90, 0.82, and 0.92, respectively. For activity grading, sensitivity was 0.82 (95% CI, 0.77-0.85), specificity 0.87 (95% CI, 0.82-0.91), and AUC 0.90 (95% CI, 0.88-0.91); after outlier exclusion, 0.80, 0.84, and 0.89, respectively. AI showed higher sensitivity than available ophthalmologist comparators for diagnosis (P = 0.01) and activity grading (P = 0.003), but comparisons involved selected readers and limited clinical context. Negative likelihood ratio was 0.09 for diagnosis and 0.21 for activity grading. PROBAST+AI rated 12.5% of diagnosis studies and 36.4% to 54.5% of activity-grading studies at high risk of bias; GRADE certainty was low.

Conclusion

Image-based AI showed promising accuracy for TED diagnosis and CAS-based activity grading. Evidence supports cautious use as a diagnosis rule-out aid under clinical supervision when negative results are interpreted with symptoms and clinical context; however, CAS-based activity grading should not rule out low-CAS active TED. Low certainty, substantial heterogeneity, and limitations of image-based comparisons preclude immediate autonomous clinical deployment. Patients with suspected TED should still be referred for ophthalmologic assessment. Prospective, multicenter, multiethnic validation is required.

records.title: Pooled Data Meta-Analysis of Pneumatic Vitreolysis for Treatment of Vitreomacular Traction Syndrome With, And Without Full Thickness Macular Holes.

content.title: Pooled Data Meta-Analysis of Pneumatic Vitreolysis for Treatment of Vitreomacular Traction Syndrome With, And Without Full Thickness Macular Holes.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To conduct a pooled data meta-analysis assessing the efficacy and complication rates of pneumatic vitreolysis as a first-line treatment for vitreomacular traction with and without full-thickness macular holes (FTMH).

Methods

The National Library of Medicine PubMed interface, EMBASE, Scopus, and Cochrane Library were queried for articles published from May 1995 to March 2025 detailing the use of a gas injection for treatment of vitreomacular traction with or without FTMH. Efficacy and complication data were pooled and analyzed.

Results

A total of 33 studies reporting on 637 eyes with VMT treated with PVL were included. Of these, 476 eyes had VMT alone and 161 had concurrent FTMH. VMT release occurred in 76% of all eyes with rates of 49%, 67%, 71%, and 83%, for filtered air, SF6, C2F6 and C3F8 respectively. Across eyes with VMT alone, the release rate was 71%, while eyes with VMT and macular holes (MH) it was 94%, and successful MH closure rate was 40%. VMT release was higher in phakic (84%) compared to pseudophakic eyes (76%). Adverse events included development of new FTMHs in 5% of VMT-only eyes, and across all studies, retinal tears and detachments developed in 8 (1%) and 13 (2%) eyes, respectively.

Conclusion

Pneumatic vitreolysis appears to be a cost-effective treatment option for patients with vitreomacular traction without FTMH with modest to good success rates. Eyes with concurrent macular hole have a modest closure rate only. The risk of complications, including FTMH, retinal tear or detachment, must be considered.

records.title: THE EFFICACY OF INTRAVITREAL ANTI-VASCULAR ENDOTHELIAL GROWTH FACTOR FOR RADIATION MACULOPATHY: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

content.title: THE EFFICACY OF INTRAVITREAL ANTI-VASCULAR ENDOTHELIAL GROWTH FACTOR FOR RADIATION MACULOPATHY: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Antivascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) therapy is the primary approach for managing radiation maculopathy. However, a noticeable gap exists in meta-analyses evaluating the efficacy of anti-VEGF therapy specifically in the context of radiation maculopathy.

Methods

We conducted a review of comparative studies on anti-VEGF treatment up to October 2023. References were sourced from PubMed, EMBASE, and the Cochrane Library. The Cochrane Risk of Bias tool assessed the quality of randomized controlled trials, while the Risk Of Bias In Nonrandomized Studies of Interventions tool evaluated nonrandomized controlled trials.

Results

Thirteen articles originating from 11 trials involving 2,525 eyes of 2,408 patients were included. Four trials with 2,226 eyes examined the effect of preventive anti-VEGF. Four trials with 189 eyes assessed the effect of anti-VEGF for preexisting maculopathy, and three trials with 110 eyes compared different anti-VEGF treatment modalities. In the preventive anti-VEGF treatment meta-analysis over a 24-month follow-up, the anti-VEGF group exhibited significantly fewer cases of radiation maculopathy (odds ratio: 0.40; 95% confidence interval: 0.25, 0.66, P = 0.0003, I 2 = 45%). For the meta-analysis of anti-VEGF treatment for preexisting radiation maculopathy over a 6-month follow-up, the anti-VEGF group showed improved visual acuity (SMD: -1.13, 95% confidence interval, -1.69 to -0.56, P < 0.0000, I 2 = 47%) and decreased central macular thickness (SMD: -0.59, 95% confidence interval, -1.13 to -0.05, P = 0.03, I 2 = 62%).

Conclusion

Prophylactic anti-VEGF effectively prevents radiation maculopathy and is also beneficial in treating preexisting radiation maculopathy. Intensive treatment initially provides early benefits, but the efficacy diminishes after transitioning to a treat-and-extend regimen.

records.title: POSTINTRAVITREAL INJECTION AND POSTCATARACT EXTRACTION ENDOPHTHALMITIS VISUAL OUTCOMES BY ORGANISM: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW AND META-ANALYSIS.

content.title: POSTINTRAVITREAL INJECTION AND POSTCATARACT EXTRACTION ENDOPHTHALMITIS VISUAL OUTCOMES BY ORGANISM: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW AND META-ANALYSIS.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To compare visual outcomes of endophthalmitis following intravitreal injections (IVIs) and cataract extraction by causative organism.

Methods

Searches in Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, MEDLINE, and Embase identified articles reporting visual outcomes by causative organisms in post-IVI and cataract extraction endophthalmitis cases from January 2010 to February 2022. A random-effects meta-analysis compared visual improvement among endophthalmitis cases caused by causative organisms.

Results

Eighty-five out of 3,317 retrieved studies were included. The highest degree of visual acuity improvement in both post-IVI and postcataract extraction endophthalmitis was seen in cases caused by coagulase-negative staphylococci, followed by gram-negative organisms and other gram-positive organisms such as streptococci and enterococci. Culture-negative cases showed more visual acuity improvement than culture-positive cases in post-IVI endophthalmitis. These results remained consistent when accounting for endophthalmitis treatment, IVI type, condition requiring IVI treatment, follow-up period, and initial preprocedural visual acuity.

Conclusion

Coagulase-negative staphylococci and gram-negative organisms show the most visual acuity improvement in both post-IVI and postcataract extraction endophthalmitis. Other gram-positive organisms such as streptococci and enterococci are associated with less visual improvement. This updated systematic review and meta-analysis revealed that the results of the Endophthalmitis Vitrectomy Study are consistent decades later despite advancements in surgical practices and the evolution of microorganisms over time.

records.title: Perspectives on the Incidence of Acanthamoeba Keratitis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

content.title: Perspectives on the Incidence of Acanthamoeba Keratitis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Topic

To provide an overview on the incidence of Acanthamoeba keratitis (AK).

Clinical relevance

Although being a sight-threatening cause of infectious keratitis, a comprehensive assessment of the incidence of AK is lacking.

Methods

Incidence of AK was computed as the number of eyes with AK per health care center, per year (annualized center incidence [ACI]). Two meta-analytical ratios also were calculated: (1) the ratio of eyes with AK to the count of eyes with nonviral microbial keratitis (MK) and (2) the ratio of eyes with AK to the overall population (i.e., the total number of people in a nation or region, as indicated by the authors in each study). Center was defined as the health care facility where the study took place. Actual and projected estimates of the number of eyes with AK in years were calculated multiplying the ratio of eyes with AK to the total population and the corresponding population estimates, sourced from the United Nations Population Prospects.

Results

Overall, 105 articles were included, published between 1987 and 2022. The total number of eyes identified was 91 951, with 5660 eyes affected by AK and 86 291 eyes affected by nonviral MK. The median ACI was 1.9 eyes with AK per health care center per year (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.5-2.6 eyes), with no statistically significant differences among continents. The ratio of eyes with AK to the total number of eyes with MK was 1.52% (95% CI, 1.03%-2.22%), whereas the ratio of eyes with AK in relationship to the entire population was estimated at 2.34 eyes per 1 000 000 people (95% CI, 0.98-5.55 per 1 000 000 people). The projected increase in the numbers of eyes with AK indicated an increase of 18.5% (n = 15 355 eyes with AK) in 2053 and 25.5% (n = 16 253 eyes with AK) in 2073, compared with the baseline of 2023 (n = 12 953 eyes with AK).

Discussion

Acanthamoeba keratitis emerged as a relatively low-incident disorder, and no significant differences in terms of its incidence were found among different continents.

Proprietary or commercial disclosure may be found in the Footnotes and Disclosures at the end of this article.

records.title: Safety and Efficacy of Half-dose and Half-fluence Photodynamic Therapy in Chronic Central Serous Chorioretinopathy: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.

content.title: Safety and Efficacy of Half-dose and Half-fluence Photodynamic Therapy in Chronic Central Serous Chorioretinopathy: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To investigate the comparative efficacy and safety of half-dose photodynamic therapy (PDT) and half-fluence PDT in the management of chronic central serous chorioretinopathy.

Design

Systematic review and meta-analysis.

Methods

A comprehensive literature search was conducted on Ovid MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Library, covering publications from January 2000 to March 2024. The review focused on studies reporting the efficacy and safety of half-dose PDT compared to half-fluence PDT in treating chronic central serous chorioretinopathy. The primary outcome was the best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) at the last study observation. Secondary outcomes included retinal thickness (RT), the presence of subretinal fluid (SRF), and SRF recurrence across follow-up visits. Random effects meta-analysis was performed using RevMan 5.4.

Results

A total of 10 studies (eight observational and two randomized controlled trials) were included in the analysis. The results indicated that half-dose PDT and half-fluence PDT achieved similar BCVA at 1 month (P = .24), 3 months (P = .40), and 6 months (P = .16). Similarly, there were no significant differences in RT at 1 month (P = .23), 3 months (P = .99), and at 6 months (P = .54) between the two treatment protocols. Both treatment protocols were associated with minor complications, indicating similar safety profiles in patients with CSCR.

Conclusions

The findings suggest that both half-dose and half-fluence PDT are effective and safe for treating CSCR, with no significant differences in BCVA, RT, or SRF resolution between the two modalities. These results support flexibility in selecting treatment based on individual patient needs. Further research with larger sample sizes and longer follow-up is required to optimize these protocols and confirm these results.

records.title: Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists and the Risk of Non-Arteritic Anterior Ischemic Optic Neuropathy: A Consensus Statement by the North American Neuro-Ophthalmology Society and the American Academy of Ophthalmology.

content.title: Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists and the Risk of Non-Arteritic Anterior Ischemic Optic Neuropathy: A Consensus Statement by the North American Neuro-Ophthalmology Society and the American Academy of Ophthalmology.
content.abstract: Recent studies have reported a possible association between glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) and non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION). The North American Neuro-Ophthalmology Society and the American Academy of Ophthalmology provide consensus expert opinion and clinical guidance about this association. Currently available evidence primarily includes retrospective observational studies, many of which rely on analysis of electronic health record and administrative claims data and are subject to limitations. Although many report a small possible increased risk of NAION in patients taking GLP-1 RAs such as semaglutide, some studies report no correlation, and the overall magnitude of the risk of NAION remains low. Shared decision-making between each patient and their care team is warranted to decide whether to start, continue, or discontinue GLP-1 RAs. FINANCIAL DISCLOSURE(S): The author(s) have no proprietary or commercial interest in any materials discussed in this article.

records.title: Postoperative Pain in Vitreoretinal Surgery With Combined Regional-General Anesthesia Versus General Anesthesia: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

content.title: Postoperative Pain in Vitreoretinal Surgery With Combined Regional-General Anesthesia Versus General Anesthesia: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To investigate postoperative pain variations in vitreoretinal surgeries conducted with combined regional-general anesthesia or general anesthesia.

Design

Systematic review and meta-analysis.

Methods

A systematic search of the PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Library databases was conducted to identify relevant randomized controlled trials published before December 26, 2023. Studies comparing vitreoretinal surgeries conducted under combined anesthesia to general anesthesia were included, while studies using only regional anesthesia were excluded. The quality of the studies was assessed using the Cochrane Collaboration risk of bias tool, and the results are presented as odds ratios or standardized mean differences (SMDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). I2 statistic was calculated to assess heterogeneity. The primary outcomes in our study included the proportions of patients needing as-needed postoperative analgesics, dosage of as-needed postoperative analgesia medications, and time to the first demand for as-needed postoperative analgesia. The secondary outcomes included postoperative pain scores at 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6, 12, 24 hours (h), duration of surgery and anesthesia, and percentage of patients experiencing postoperative nausea and vomiting.

Results

A total of 19 randomized controlled trials involving 1314 patients were analyzed. Combined anesthesia was associated with lower proportions of patients needing as-needed postoperative analgesics (odds ratio, 0.218 95% CI, 0.114-0.418, I2 = 55.2%), reduced dosage of as-needed postoperative analgesia medications (SMD, -1.429, 95% CI, -2.395 to -0.462, I2 = 90.4%), and longer time to the first demand for as-needed postoperative analgesia compared with general anesthesia alone (SMD, 2.650, 95% CI, 1.169-4.132, I2 = 96.5%). The effect of additional regional anesthesia lasted for 6 h (0.5 h SMD, -1.471, 95% CI, -2.498 to -0.444, I2 = 90.5%; 1 h, -1.507, -2.309 to -0.705, 92.7%; 2 h -1.487, -2.300 to -0.674, 93.2%; 4 h -1.052, -1.708 to -0.396, 89.5%; 6 h -1.053, -1.932 to -0.174, 93.4%; 12 h -0.286, -0.648 to 0.076, 57.1%; 24 h -0.297, -0.624 to 0.029, 64.0%). Combined anesthesia decreased postoperative nausea and vomiting risk without affecting the surgical or anesthesia duration.

Conclusions

Combined anesthesia demonstrated additional postoperative analgesic effects versus general anesthesia only. Further research is needed to validate the results of our study and to identify vision-threatening complications.

records.title: Seeing in tandem: Cis and trans-regulation of tandemly-duplicated cone opsin genes in zebrafish.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Seeing in tandem: Cis and trans-regulation of tandemly-duplicated cone opsin genes in zebrafish.
content.abstract: The molecular basis for vertebrate color vision is expression of spectrally-selective opsin-based photopigments within distinct cone photoreceptor populations. In several primates including humans, and in numerous fish species, genes encoding duplicated, spectrally-divergent cone opsin proteins may be positioned in tandem arrays. This article reviews studies of the regulation of differential expression of these duplicated cone opsin genes in humans and fish, with an emphasis on knowledge derived from the zebrafish model. In humans, the long wavelength-sensitive/medium wavelength-sensitive (LWS/MWS; red/green) tandemly-duplicated array underlies trichromatic color vision; mutations in this array cause altered color vision and retinal degenerations. A foundational model posited that regulation of human LWS vs. MWS opsin expression is stochastic, whereby an upstream enhancer associates randomly with promoters of the proximal or distal gene, and one of these associations becomes permanent. Discoveries of tandemly-duplicated cone opsin genes in teleost fish, including the versatile zebrafish model, led to their use to further pursue mechanisms of differential expression. The tandemly-duplicated zebrafish lws1 and lws2 genes (encoding red-sensing cone opsins) share a common ancestral gene with human LWS and MWS. Subsequent studies revealed that differential expression of these genes is regulated by the paracrine signal retinoic acid (RA) and the endocrine signal thyroid hormone (TH). Further investigations identified additional cone transcripts distinguishing zebrafish LWS1 vs. LWS2 cones, plasticity of cone opsin expression across the lifespan in response to TH, and a candidate receptor and cis-regulatory element. The findings warrant updates to the foundational model and further consideration of hypotheses for regulation of the human LWS vs. MWS genes.

records.title: Effectiveness, Stability, and Influence Factors of Femtosecond Laser-Assisted Arcuate Keratotomy in Cataract Surgery: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

content.title: Effectiveness, Stability, and Influence Factors of Femtosecond Laser-Assisted Arcuate Keratotomy in Cataract Surgery: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness, stability, and influencing factors of femtosecond laser-assisted arcuate keratotomy (FSAK) performed during cataract surgery for correcting corneal astigmatism (CA).

Methods

A systematic literature review was conducted to identify clinical trials adopting a pre-post study design. Data sources included electronic databases such as PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase. Corneal astigmatism was assessed preoperatively and at multiple postoperative intervals: 1 month, 3 months, 6 months, and 1 year. Comparative analyses were conducted to determine the efficacy and stability over time. Subgroup analyses of CA reduction and absolute angle of error were performed based on potential influence factors including the type, depth, diameter, and platform of FSAK, magnitude and type of preoperative CA, and area of the study. Statistical analyses were performed using Review Manager 5.4.

Design

Systematic review and meta-analysis.

Results

Of the 40 articles initially identified, 20 met the final inclusion criteria. Follow-up durations ranged from 1 month to 2 years. Significant reduction in CA postoperative were observed at 1 month, 3 months, 6 months, and 1 year after surgery (mean difference [MD] = -0.55 D, -0.66 D, -0.43 D, and -0.67 D, respectively; all P < .02). CA between different postoperative time points were not significant (all P > .20). Subgroup analysis did not address the high heterogeneity. However, differences of CA reduction between subgroups based on type, depth, diameter, and platform of FSAK were significant. Penetrating FSAK, deeper incision, optical diameter at 8.5 mm were shown to introduce higher CA reduction (P = .005, .02, < .001, respectively). The effect achieved by different laser platforms were significantly different (P = .0002).

Conclusions

FSAK performed during cataract surgery effectively reduces corneal astigmatism, with stability observed from 1 month to 1 year postoperatively. The corrective performance is closely related to type, depth, diameter, and platform of FSAK. This study was supported by the National Natural Science Foundation of China (Grant No. 82171039 and No. 82301191).

Registration number

PROSPERO CRD 42024504481).

records.title: Ocular changes in human spaceflight.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Ocular changes in human spaceflight.
content.abstract: Spaceflight presents unique challenges to ocular health, with astronauts experiencing a range of visual disturbances in the setting of microgravity, radiation exposure, and other environmental factors. This review synthesizes knowledge about how spaceflight affects ocular anatomy and function. We outline the diagnostic and therapeutic limitations in microgravity, including constraints on imaging modalities, intracranial pressure measurement, and drug delivery. In addition, we examine common spaceflight-associated ocular pathologies, including spaceflight-associated neuro-ocular syndrome, corneal epithelial disruption, possible radiation-associated lens changes, and retinal or choroidal alterations. Drawing from evidence across human missions, terrestrial analogs, and experimental models, this review emphasizes the critical importance of vision to astronaut safety and mission success. Future directions include long-term ocular health monitoring, advancement of in-flight diagnostic capabilities, and multidisciplinary strategies to safeguard astronaut vision.

records.title: Comparison of Renal Adverse Events Between Intravitreal Anti-Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor Agents: A Meta-Analysis.

content.title: Comparison of Renal Adverse Events Between Intravitreal Anti-Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor Agents: A Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To compare the risk of renal adverse events, particularly acute kidney injury (AKI), between intravitreal anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) agents.

Design

Meta-analysis.

Methods

A systematic literature search was conducted on Ovid Medline, Embase, and the Cochrane Library for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) published from January 2005 to February 2024 involving adult patients receiving anti-VEGF intravitreal injections for age-related macular degeneration, diabetic macular edema, and macular edema secondary to retinal vein occlusion. The primary outcome was the comparative risk of AKI between anti-VEGF agents and sham injections. Secondary outcomes involved other renal adverse events. Subgroup analyses were conducted by specific disease indications. A random-effects model was used for meta-analysis to estimate risk ratios (RRs) and their 95% confidence intervals, with a P value of <.05 representing statistical significance. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (ROB2) tool, and the certainty of evidence was evaluated through the Cochrane Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) framework.

Results

A total of 10,031 eyes from 11 RCTs were included. No significant differences were found in the risk of acute or chronic renal conditions, obstructive uropathies, neoplasia, or infectious processes between anti-VEGF agents and sham therapy. AKI was reported in 5.4% (n = 10/185) of patients treated with bevacizumab, 1.3% (n = 6/456) with sham, 1.0% (n = 48/4724) with aflibercept, 0.8% (n = 15/1929) with faricimab, 0.5% (n = 5/1098) with brolucizumab, and 0.3% (n = 5/1639) with ranibizumab. No significant differences in AKI risk were observed between any of the anti-VEGF agents and sham (P > .05 for all comparisons). However, there was an increased risk of patient-reported symptoms with 1.25 mg bevacizumab compared to 2 mg aflibercept (RR = 3.26, 95% CI = 1.07-9.93, P = .04), driven primarily by reports of hematuria: 4.3% (bevacizumab), 0.7% (sham), 0.2% (aflibercept), 0.1% (faricimab), and 0.1% (ranibizumab).

Conclusions

US Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved intravitreal anti-VEGF agents do not significantly increase the risk of AKI compared to sham injections. Nevertheless, variations in patient-reported renal symptoms were observed across different anti-VEGF drugs. These variations were influenced primarily by differences in hematuria events, which may be a result of differential systemic absorption by these agents. These results underscore the importance of continuous monitoring and pharmacovigilance.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence in Endodontics: A Narrative Review and Critical Synthesis of Diagnostic, Predictive, and Operational Applications.

content.title: Artificial Intelligence in Endodontics: A Narrative Review and Critical Synthesis of Diagnostic, Predictive, and Operational Applications.
content.abstract: Background/Objectives: Artificial intelligence (AI) research in endodontics has grown quickly, but the strength of the evidence differs between applications. This narrative review with structured evidence mapping examined diagnostic imaging, canal morphology, outcome prediction, large language models (LLMs), robotics and augmented reality, and operational uses such as case-difficulty assessment, triage and scheduling. Methods: Two anchor reviews were combined with a documented PubMed search to 30 September 2026, and studies were classified by design, sample, reference standard, validation, and evidence of clinical utility. Results: Periapical lesion detection has the largest evidence base: one meta-analysis reported pooled sensitivity of 0.925 and specificity of 0.852, although most included studies were at risk of bias and none was prospective. Fracture detection relies mainly on ex vivo data and is sensitive to image resolution. Outcome models showed modest to moderate discrimination in single-centre data. LLM studies reported 40% to 100% correct, appropriate, or concordant responses across different benchmarks and scoring rules, and outputs varied on repeated querying. Difficulty-assessment and scheduling tools have appeared since 2020 but have not been evaluated prospectively in clinical workflow. Conclusions: Technical performance has not yet been shown to translate into clinical benefit, and AI in endodontics should currently be used only as clinician-supervised decision support.

records.title: Assessment of peripapillary choroidal microvascular structure in idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus using a deep learning-based approach.
records.publisher: Graefe's archive for clinical and experimental ophthalmology = Albrecht von Graefes Archiv fur klinische und experimentelle Ophthalmologie

content.title: Assessment of peripapillary choroidal microvascular structure in idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus using a deep learning-based approach.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To investigate peripapillary choroidal microvascular structure in patients with idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus (iNPH) using a novel deep learning-based approach, and to evaluate longitudinal changes following shunt surgery.

Methods

In this prospective study, 22 patients with iNPH and 22 age-matched healthy controls underwent peripapillary optical coherence tomography (OCT). A deep learning-based ResUNet model enabled choroidal segmentation and quantification of total choroidal area (TCA), stromal choroidal area (SCA), luminal choroidal area (LCA), and the choroidal vascularity index (CVI). Measurements were compared between groups and reassessed in iNPH patients after ventriculoperitoneal shunt surgery.

Results

Forty-four eyes of 22 iNPH patients and 44 eyes of 22 controls were analyzed. iNPH eyes exhibited significantly greater mean SCA compared to controls (adjusted p < 0.05). On the other hand, CVI remained comparable between groups. Following a mean follow-up of approximately 12 months after shunt surgery, mean SCA showed significant reduction (adjusted p < 0.05), whereas CVI remained unchanged.

Conclusions

iNPH was associated with peripapillary choroidal changes, predominantly involving the stromal compartment. Deep learning-based OCT analysis may provide a noninvasive approach for quantifying peripapillary choroidal microstructure, although the clinical relevance of these findings remains to be established.

records.title: Early Diagnosis and Prognosis of Corneal and Ocular Surface Pathologies Using Artificial Intelligence: A State-of-the-art Review.

content.title: Early Diagnosis and Prognosis of Corneal and Ocular Surface Pathologies Using Artificial Intelligence: A State-of-the-art Review.
content.abstract:
Purpose

This study aims to elucidate the expanding role of artificial intelligence (AI) in the early diagnosis of corneal and ocular surface diseases. AI has the potential to enhance diagnostic precision, streamline clinical workflows, and facilitate disease detection before clinical manifestations become evident.

Methods

A narrative literature review was conducted to assess the impact of AI and machine learning in corneal disease preclinical diagnosis. A comprehensive search in PubMed was performed using key terms such as "artificial intelligence," "machine learning," "deep learning," "corneal diseases," and "early diagnosis." Eligible studies were those published in English over the last decade that focused on AI-driven diagnostic approaches and prognostic modeling. Case reports, nonoriginal studies, and those with minimal AI integration were excluded. Data extraction emphasized AI methodologies, imaging techniques, diagnostic performance metrics, and clinical relevance.

Results

AI-powered machine learning models analyze vast imaging datasets, detecting subclinical abnormalities imperceptible to conventional diagnostic methods. This capability is particularly significant in early keratoconus detection, dystrophies, infectious keratitis, conjunctival neoplasia, and other corneal pathologies such as dry eye or Steven-Johnson disease, where subtle morphological changes precede clinically apparent disease.

Conclusions

The integration of AI into corneal disease diagnostics and management could mark in the future a transformative shift in Ophthalmology, offering precision, efficiency, and scalability. By facilitating early disease detection and individualized patient assessments, AI minimizes diagnostic inconsistencies and accelerates clinical decision making. Continuous algorithm refinement and real-world validation are crucial to maximizing AI's clinical utility. To fully harness AI's potential, multidisciplinary collaboration among ophthalmologists, data scientists, and regulatory bodies is imperative to address standardization, ethical concerns, and implementation barriers. As AI-driven technologies continue to evolve, they will redefine the standard of care in corneal disease diagnosis, therapeutic precision, and patient outcomes.

records.title: Automating systematic reviews in ophthalmology with the use of large language model deep research tools.

content.title: Automating systematic reviews in ophthalmology with the use of large language model deep research tools.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the performance of large language model (LLM) 'Deep Research' agentic systems for writing systematic reviews (SRs) in ophthalmology.

Methods

Structured prompts were submitted in September 2026 to Deep Research tools powered by GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 to produce SRs on the topics of 50 human-authored SRs published between May and August 2026 in ophthalmology journals (2025 Journal Impact Factor ≥ 3). Main outcomes included literature coverage (recall and precision against the studies included in the human-made SRs on the same topics), data extraction accuracy (discrepant numerical findings against cited sources), percentage of valid references and PRISMA adherence.

Results

One hundred SRs were produced, 50 for each LLM. Both LLMs showed limited overlap with the human-made SRs, with similar recall (38.0% vs. 38.3%; p = 0.859) and higher precision for GPT-6 Astra (53.2% vs. 36.8%; p < 0.001). GPT-6 Astra achieved a lower data reporting error rate (0.2%) compared to Claude Fable 5.1 (0.9%) (p < 0.001). The percentage of valid references was lower for GPT-6 Astra (79.2% vs. 91.4%; p < 0.001). PRISMA adherence was suboptimal for both models (50.2% vs. 55.2% of items fulfilled; p < 0.001).

Conclusion

GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 showed low data reporting error rates in evidence synthesis; however, incomplete literature coverage, bibliography management issues and poor adherence to reporting guidelines mandate human oversight, especially in study selection and quality appraisal.

records.title: Global Research Trends at the Intersection of Macular Degeneration and Refractive Error: A Bibliometric and Visual Analysis.

content.title: Global Research Trends at the Intersection of Macular Degeneration and Refractive Error: A Bibliometric and Visual Analysis.
content.abstract:
Objective

This study aimed to examine the publication patterns, collaborative networks, and thematic developments at the intersection of macular degeneration and refractive error using a bibliometric analysis.

Methods and analysis

A comprehensive search of the Web of Science Core Collection (SCI-Expanded and SSCI) was conducted from 1 January 2004 to 31 December 2024. The search combined keywords for macular degeneration (e.g., "AMD," "choroidal neovascularization") and refractive error (e.g., "myopia," "hypermetropia"). After screening, 1,716 peer-reviewed English-language publications were included. CiteSpace (v6.3.R3) and VOSviewer (v1.6.20) were used for collaboration networks, co-citation maps, and keyword co-occurrence analysis. Microsoft Excel supported descriptive statistics.

Results

A total of 1,716 publications were included. Publication output increased markedly after 2016 and peaked in 2024. China contributed the most publications, while the United States showed the highest citation count and total link strength. Jost B. Jonas and Kyoko Ohno-Matsui were the most productive authors. Keyword analysis showed growing interest in artificial intelligence, deep learning, and myopia control alongside established treatment and imaging topics. Citation-based comparisons for recent years should be interpreted cautiously because these publications have had shorter citation windows.

Conclusions

Macular degeneration and refractive error research has grown substantially over the past two decades. China leads in output, while the United States leads in citation impact and collaboration strength. This gap suggests that publication volume does not always translate into research influence. Artificial intelligence has emerged as a rising direction. These findings may help researchers identify collaboration opportunities and future priorities.

records.title: Clinical Utility and Limitations of Sub-Basal Corneal Nerve Imaging Using Confocal Microscopy in Systemic Diseases.

content.title: Clinical Utility and Limitations of Sub-Basal Corneal Nerve Imaging Using Confocal Microscopy in Systemic Diseases.
content.abstract: Corneal confocal microscopy (CCM), also referred to as in vivo confocal microscopy, is a non-invasive ophthalmic imaging technique that allows real-time visualization of the sub-basal nerve plexus and epithelial dendritic cells in the living cornea. Initially used for the diagnosis of anterior segment disorders, it has been increasingly applied to the evaluation of small-fiber involvement in systemic conditions, particularly diabetic peripheral neuropathy, in which CCM-derived parameters correlate with intraepidermal nerve fiber density (IENFD) on skin biopsy. This narrative review summarizes the technical principles of CCM, image-analysis approaches from manual tracing to deep learning, and the clinical evidence in peripheral neuropathies, central neurodegenerative diseases, autoimmune and inflammatory conditions, and long COVID. Outside diabetes, however, most data come from small, single-center, cross-sectional studies. Four barriers currently prevent CCM from becoming a routine clinical biomarker: (i) the absence of validated diagnostic thresholds and age-adjusted normative ranges outside diabetic neuropathy; (ii) the lack of disease specificity, as similar nerve loss occurs in many neurological, metabolic and ocular surface conditions; (iii) limited comparability across devices, acquisition protocols, image selection and analysis software, with automated and deep-learning tools still lacking multicenter external validation; and (iv) cost, contact-based acquisition and operator training. Overcoming these barriers will require standardized acquisition and reporting, open benchmark datasets, externally validated analysis pipelines, and large prospective longitudinal cohorts.

records.title: Choosing the Right AI Model for Uveal Melanoma From Detection to Prognosis.

content.title: Choosing the Right AI Model for Uveal Melanoma From Detection to Prognosis.
content.abstract: Ocular oncology sits in an unusual position for medical artificial intelligence (AI), imaging heavy and multimodal by nature, but constrained by the rarity of the tumours it treats. Uveal melanoma, the most common primary intraocular malignancy in adults, accounts for approximately 7095 new cases worldwide each year. Choroidal naevi are present in approximately 5% of the white population aged 40 and over, of which roughly 1 in 8845 transforms into melanoma each year, leaving a large benign population within which a small number of melanomas must not be missed. This narrative review follows the uveal melanoma clinical pathway through detection, diagnosis and prognosis, asking at each stage which class of AI model the evidence supports. A structured PubMed search returned 176 unique records, from which 29 primary studies were included, 17 (59%) published in 2025 or 2026. At detection, heavy self-supervised foundation models generalise well across imaging hardware but lack calibration to a clinical decision, while lightweight purpose-built classifiers show the opposite trade-off, and only one tool has been tested in a real referral workflow, quadrupling the odds of correct referral and cutting false positives 10-fold. At diagnosis, purpose-built convolutional classifiers calibrated to a referral threshold remain most mature, reaching 0.88 AUC on two cohorts, while multimodal fusion claims rest on a single 0.01 AUC gain. At prognosis, biomarker prediction from routine pathology reaches 0.93 to 0.99 AUC, survival prediction lags, only 7 of 29 studies (24%) had external validation and none of the tools has regulatory clearance.

records.title: The association between large language model dependence and academic anxiety among nursing students: statistical indirect associations through artificial intelligence addiction and academic burnout.

content.title: The association between large language model dependence and academic anxiety among nursing students: statistical indirect associations through artificial intelligence addiction and academic burnout.
content.abstract:
Background

Increasing use of large language models in nursing education has raised questions about the association between reliance on these tools and academic distress. This study examined direct and specific indirect associations between large language model dependence (LMD) and academic anxiety (AA) through artificial intelligence addiction (AIA) and academic burnout (AB).

Methods

A cross-sectional survey was conducted from March to April 2026 among 473 nursing students in Guangdong Province, China, including students undertaking clinical placements. The four constructs were assessed using items selected from published self-report instruments. Partial least squares structural equation modeling was performed with age and sex included as covariates. Direct and specific indirect associations were evaluated using bootstrapping with 5,000 resamples.

Results

Cronbach's α ranged from 0.914 to 0.944, composite reliability from 0.935 to 0.954, and average variance extracted from 0.560 to 0.721. Heterotrait-monotrait ratios ranged from 0.485 to 0.733, supporting discriminant validity. Model fit evidence was mixed: SRMR was 0.068, whereas NFI was 0.812, below the 0.90 reference value. The model explained 49.2% of the variance in academic anxiety. Large language model dependence showed a small positive direct association with academic anxiety (β = 0.138, 95% CI [0.006, 0.278], p = 0.048). Significant specific indirect associations were identified through academic burnout (β = 0.205, 95% CI [0.123, 0.303]) and through artificial intelligence addiction followed by academic burnout (β = 0.098, 95% CI [0.049, 0.147]); both p < 0.001.

Conclusion

Large language model dependence was positively associated with academic anxiety among nursing students, with specific indirect associations through academic burnout and through artificial intelligence addiction followed by academic burnout. These findings highlight the relevance of problematic AI use and study-related exhaustion to academic distress. However, the cross-sectional design does not establish temporal ordering or causal mediation.

records.title: Annotation-Free Vision-Language Concept Bottleneck Models for Interpretable Medical Image Classification: A Review.

content.title: Annotation-Free Vision-Language Concept Bottleneck Models for Interpretable Medical Image Classification: A Review.
content.abstract: Concept Bottleneck Models (CBMs) route predictions through a layer of human-understandable concepts, but classical CBMs need a concept label for every training image, a cost that is high in medicine. Vision-language models (VLMs) remove that requirement because, in a shared image-text embedding space, a large language model can propose candidate concepts and contrastive similarity can score them, with no concept labels. This review surveys annotation-free VLM-based CBMs and their move into clinical imaging. We cover vision-language foundations (CLIP, ALIGN, LLaVA) and trace concept models from early supervised methods (CBM, CEM, TCAV) to versions that work without manual labels (LaBo, Label-Free CBM, PCBM, OpenCBM, VLG-CBM). We then map these foundations to specific medical fields such as radiology, pathology, cardiology, dermatology, and ophthalmology, highlighting the medical VLM-CBMs closest to actual deployment (CBVLM, AdaCBM, ConcepPath, CBM-RAG). We focus on information leakage, in which task information reaches the prediction through the concept layer without being carried by the named concepts. Two of the seven surveyed medical VLM-CBMs test whether their predictions depend on individual concepts, but none measures leakage, and no shared protocol exists. We identify this gap as a central challenge for interpretable medical AI.

records.title: Association between deep-learning-derived retinal aging speed and rapid decline of renal function in the Japanese general population.

content.title: Association between deep-learning-derived retinal aging speed and rapid decline of renal function in the Japanese general population.
content.abstract:
Background

The eye and the kidney share microvascular features, and retinal changes have been postulated to reflect systemic cardiometabolic dysfunction. Recently, retinal age, estimated by deep learning (DL) from a single fundus photograph, has been shown to predict cardiovascular events. The present study aimed to determine whether retinal aging speed, defined as the individual-specific annual rate of change in DL-estimated retinal age, is associated with rapid estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) decline.

Methods

We retrospectively analyzed the longitudinal data obtained from 7807 Japanese individuals who underwent repeated health check-ups with serial measurements of eGFR and fundus photographs (median 9.0 visits over median 8.0 years). We evaluated the relationship between retinal aging speed during the baseline period (from baseline to year 4) and rapid eGFR decline (≤ -3 ml/min/1.73 m²/year) during the follow-up period (after year 4).

Results

The incidence of rapid eGFR decline was significantly higher in the highest quartile of retinal aging speed than in the lowest quartile as the reference group in the fully adjusted model adjusting age, sex, body mass index, blood pressure, diabetes, smoking, eGFR, and proteinuria [odds ratio (OR) 1.34; 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.06-1.68; P = .015]. In the multivariable logistic regression models, retinal aging speed was associated with rapid eGFR decline after adjusting multiple key confounders (OR 1.14; 95% CI 1.02-1.29; P = .027).

Conclusions

Taken together, DL-derived retinal aging speed is independently associated with rapid eGFR decline in the Japanese general population.

records.title: Mapping Research on AI-Based Computer-Aided Diagnosis and Clinical Decision Support Systems: a Bibliometric Study Integrating Google Trends and Content Analysis.

content.title: Mapping Research on AI-Based Computer-Aided Diagnosis and Clinical Decision Support Systems: a Bibliometric Study Integrating Google Trends and Content Analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Research on artificial intelligence-based computer-aided diagnosis and clinical decision support systems (AI-CDSS) is expanding, but integrated evidence on publication patterns, keyword trajectories, online search activity, and methodological characteristics remains limited.

Objective

To characterize AI-CDSS research by integrating bibliometric analysis, Google Trends comparison, and structured content analysis of citation-ranked publications.

Methods

Scholarly interest was assessed using bibliometric analysis of Web of Science records from 2016 through August 2026, including author-keyword co-occurrence, bibliographic coupling, and reference co-citation, whereas Google Trends was used to characterize online search activity. A structured content analysis of citation-ranked publications was conducted to examine applications, methodological characteristics, and reported limitations.

Results

We analyzed 19,809 included publications from 2016 through August 2026. Output rose approximately 21-fold, from 193 records in 2016 to 4,082 in 2025. Output was geographically concentrated within the included corpus, with a Gini coefficient of 0.869. Among records with identifiable corresponding-author country or territory, China, the United States, and India accounted for 61.33%. Scientific Reports was the most frequent source (n = 916). Frequent artificial intelligence- and diagnosis-related keywords included machine learning (n = 5,666), deep learning (n = 4,022), and computer-aided diagnosis (n = 1,512). Bibliographic coupling identified 15 publication communities, and reference co-citation identified seven reference communities. In the monthly level-series comparison, 9 of 10 keyword concepts exhibited significant associations with Google Trends relative search interest, but none of the 10 first-difference associations remained significant after Bonferroni adjustment. Content analysis of 215 citation-ranked publications, including 191 empirical publications, showed frequent use of convolutional neural networks in diagnostic and radiology applications. Common limitations included limited external validation, infrequent calibration reporting, and sparse workflow-level or impact evaluation.

Conclusion

AI-CDSS research has rapidly expanded around machine learning, deep learning, and diagnostic applications, but the analyzed citation-ranked publications provide more evidence of methodological development than of clinical deployment. Integrating bibliometric, search-activity, and content-based perspectives shows limited short-term correspondence between online search activity and scholarly keyword use and highlights the need to move beyond model development toward independent external validation, prospective workflow and patient-outcome evaluation, calibration, fairness, and postdeployment monitoring.

records.title: Automated assessment of healthcare de-escalation communication skills in a conversational AI virtual reality simulation.

content.title: Automated assessment of healthcare de-escalation communication skills in a conversational AI virtual reality simulation.
content.abstract:
Introduction

Digital health training environments increasingly require scalable methods for assessing communication skills in realistic, interactive scenarios. This paper presents a comparative study of automated assessment approaches within a conversational AI virtual reality simulation designed for verbal de-escalation training.

Methods

A total of 20 nursing students completed the simulation, where their spoken responses were captured and converted to text through a speech-to-text system, and were evaluated across 11 de-escalation competencies. The evaluation compared three fine-tuned deep learning models (BERT, RoBERTa, and XLNet) with a modified RATAS, a rubric-driven framework that leverages large language models. Two experiments were conducted: one using controlled 100-item validation datasets for each section, and another using the real-world responses collected during the user study.

Results

On the validation datasets, the deep learning models achieved the highest performance, with RoBERTa obtaining an average accuracy of 0.9927, followed by BERT at 0.9900 and XLNet at 0.9790, while RATAS achieved 0.8554. On the student-response dataset, performance decreased for all approaches, with RoBERTa obtaining 0.8590 accuracy, RATAS 0.8181, BERT 0.8000, and XLNet 0.7681.

Discussion

These results suggest that transformer-based models perform best under controlled conditions, whereas RATAS demonstrated stability in grading across different dataset types. These preliminary findings support the feasibility of integrating deep learning and rubric-driven LLM-based automated assessment approaches for communication and de-escalation training in nursing education.

records.title: Global research trends of artificial intelligence in echocardiography (1984-2025): a bibliometric analysis.

content.title: Global research trends of artificial intelligence in echocardiography (1984-2025): a bibliometric analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Echocardiography has evolved substantially since its introduction in 1954. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers transformative potential for image acquisition, quantification, interpretation, and reporting. Despite growing research interest, a comprehensive evaluation of the historical trends and evolution of AI in echocardiography is lacking. The study aimed to conduct a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of the global research landscape in this field.

Methods

A systematic literature search was conducted using the Scopus and Web of Science Core Collection databases for publications on AI in echocardiography from inception through November 10, 2025; no language filter was applied. Data analysis was performed using Microsoft Excel, Microsoft Access, and IBM SPSS Statistics. In addition, bibliometric mapping and data visualization were conducted.

Results

Overall, 2682 publications received 35,083 citations (mean, 13.08 citations per publication), spanning 1984-2025. Original articles, conference papers, and review articles accounted for 87.4% and 98.5% of total publications and citations, respectively. Publication output remained limited until approximately 2015, rose gradually thereafter, and accelerated markedly after 2018, with similar output in 2024 and 2025. The United States led in both publication volume and total citations, followed by China and the United Kingdom. The United States also had the highest collaboration link strength, and seven of the top 10 institutions were in North America (six in the United States and one in Canada). Mayo Clinic ranked first, with 142 publications and 3604 citations, and had the earliest first indexed publication among the top institutions (1992). The journal JACC: Cardiovascular Imaging ranked first in both total citations (1,911) and citations per publication (36.75). "Echocardiography," "deep learning," "artificial intelligence," and "machine learning" were the most frequently used terms. The thematic evolution showed continuity of algorithmic-centric themes (1984-2019) with emerging clinically oriented themes (2020-2025).

Conclusions

This comprehensive bibliometric analysis highlights the rapid expansion of AI research in echocardiography, characterized by an accelerating publication output and emerging clinically oriented research topics. These findings reflect growing research interest in integrating AI into echocardiographic practice and highlight the need for future research prioritizing multicenter validation, clinical translation, and equitable real-world implementation.

records.title: Artificial intelligence and machine learning: Shaping the future of venous thromboembolism diagnosis and prognosis.

content.title: Artificial intelligence and machine learning: Shaping the future of venous thromboembolism diagnosis and prognosis.
content.abstract:
Background

Venous thromboembolism (VTE) continues to pose a substantial health issue worldwide, characterized by high rates of mortality and morbidity. The field of artificial intelligence (AI) has shown potential as a valuable asset for enhancing the detection and prediction of complex diseases, such as VTE.

Methods

This review explores the role of AI in VTE prediction and diagnosis, analyzing various machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) approaches, including natural language processing (NLP), support vector machines (SVM), random forests (RF), logistic regression (LR), gradient boosting methods, and deep learning frameworks such as ClotCatcher.

Results

Among the artificial intelligence models, those based on natural language processing algorithms, particularly ClotCatcher, demonstrated strong performance in analyzing unstructured clinical data. ClotCatcher achieved exceptional Area under the Curve (AUC) values of 0.980 and 0.995 for venous thromboembolism (VTE) adjudication from radiology reports. AI-driven methodologies facilitate early detection, personalized risk assessment, and enhanced patient outcomes.

Conclusion

AI holds great potential for improving VTE diagnosis and risk assessment, offering greater accuracy and efficiency than traditional methods. However, further studies are required to validate these models across diverse populations and clinical environments. The integration of AI in VTE management represents a promising frontier in personalized medicine, potentially leading to improved outcomes and more efficient healthcare delivery.

records.title: Beyond scales: Artificial intelligence, language, and behavior in suicide risk modeling-a narrative review.
records.publisher: European neuropsychopharmacology : the journal of the European College of Neuropsychopharmacology

content.title: Beyond scales: Artificial intelligence, language, and behavior in suicide risk modeling-a narrative review.
content.abstract: Suicide is a leading, preventable cause of premature mortality, yet identifying individuals at imminent risk remains difficult. There are no validated biomarkers for routine stratification, and common approaches (clinical interviews, rating scales, self-report) are limited by subjectivity, reporting bias, and weak positive predictive value for rare outcomes. Rapid advances in artificial intelligence (AI)-including machine learning, deep learning, and large language models-offer opportunities to integrate heterogeneous signals relevant to risk and treatment response. This narrative review summarizes recent AI-enabled prediction and characterization of suicidal thoughts and behaviors across major data modalities: structured electronic health records and claims; natural language processing of clinical notes and digital text; speech and facial/behavioral signals; neuroimaging and other neurobiological measures; and passive sensing from smartphones and wearables. We review common modeling and evaluation practices, emphasizing clinically relevant performance assessment (discrimination and calibration) and the importance of temporal and external validation. We also highlight barriers to translation, including class imbalance and label noise, dataset shift across sites and time, limited prospective evaluation, and the need for interpretable outputs that can support medication decisions and care pathways (e.g., triage, monitoring, and stepped interventions). Ethical and implementation challenges-privacy and consent, algorithmic bias and equity, governance, and the clinical consequences of false-positive and false-negative predictions-are discussed with an emphasis on safe deployment. We conclude with priorities for the field, including multimodal longitudinal cohorts, harmonized reporting standards, and pragmatic trials to determine whether AI decision support measurably improves suicide-prevention outcomes.

records.title: Application of an Artificial Intelligence Simulated Patient Model in Teaching Neurosurgical Decision-Making.

content.title: Application of an Artificial Intelligence Simulated Patient Model in Teaching Neurosurgical Decision-Making.
content.abstract:
Aim

Training in neurosurgical decision-making remains a challenging component of standardized residency training. Traditional teaching models are limited in their ability to simulate the uncertainty and complexity encountered in real-world clinical scenarios. As a novel educational tool, the potential value of artificial intelligence (AI)-simulated patient models in surgical decision-making training requires further evaluation. This study aimed to explore the application of an AI-simulated patient model in neurosurgical decision-making education and to assess its effectiveness in improving residents' clinical decision-making abilities.

Methods

A retrospective study was conducted involving 157 residents who underwent standardized residency training in the Department of Neurosurgery from January 2023 to April 2026. Based on the implementation of the AI-simulated teaching model beginning in January 2025, participants were divided into two groups according to the teaching model used: an experimental group (n = 72, receiving AI-simulated patient teaching from January 2025 to April 2026) and a control group (n = 85, receiving traditional case discussion teaching from January 2023 to December 2024). The experimental group used a large language model-based virtual patient system powered by DeepSeek to perform dialogue-driven history taking, image interpretation, surgical planning, and risk prediction with real-time feedback, while the control group received conventional methods. After teaching, an objective structured clinical examination (OSCE) was used to assess surgical decision-making across five dimensions, including localization diagnosis, surgical approach, risk identification, emergency management, and surgical timing, and a questionnaire was used to measure teaching satisfaction.

Results

The total score for surgical decision-making ability was significantly higher in the experimental group than in the control group (p < 0.001). Dimensional analysis showed that localization diagnosis, surgical method selection, risk identification, emergency response, and surgical timing judgment were higher in the experimental group than in the control group (all p < 0.05). The excellent rate for each assessment dimension (>85 points) was significantly higher in the experimental group than in the control group (p < 0.05). The satisfaction score was also higher in the experimental group than in the control group (p < 0.001).

Conclusions

The AI-simulated patient model based on a general-purpose large language model was associated with better surgical decision-making performance among neurosurgery residents. It has significant advantages in localization diagnosis, surgical approach selection, risk identification, emergency response, and judgment of surgical timing, and is well accepted by residents.

records.title: Beyond the Chatbot: Agentic Artificial Intelligence and the Future of Infectious Disease Practice.
records.publisher: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America

content.title: Beyond the Chatbot: Agentic Artificial Intelligence and the Future of Infectious Disease Practice.
content.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) discourse in infectious disease (ID) has focused on benchmarking large language model chatbots against clinicians, a useful but narrowing inquiry. Agentic AI is a different paradigm: goal-directed systems that pursue clinical objectives over time, integrating data, invoking tools, monitoring results, and adapting without repeated prompting. This Viewpoint defines the anatomy of an agent, situates it within a 3-level framework (predictive, conversational, agentic), and examines how agents could transform 6 domains of ID practice: clinical care, antimicrobial stewardship, clinical microbiology, infection prevention and control, research, and epidemiology and pandemic preparedness. Individual components have proven value; integrated systems remain untested. No validated agentic system has been deployed in clinical ID; error propagation, algorithmic bias, cost, absent validation frameworks, undefined liability, and consequences for the workforce and its training must be addressed first. The ID community has a narrow window to shape these systems before decisions are made without it.

records.title: Impact of Image Bit Depth Reduction on Deep Learning Performance in Chest Radiograph Analysis: A Multi-institutional Study.

content.title: Impact of Image Bit Depth Reduction on Deep Learning Performance in Chest Radiograph Analysis: A Multi-institutional Study.
content.abstract:
Rationale and objectives

Medical imaging typically generates 12-bit to 16-bit formats, yet conversion to 8-bit is often required. While deep learning has been widely explored in medical imaging, the influence of image bit depth on model performance is not fully understood. This study evaluates the impact of conversion from 16-bit to 8-bit for sex, age, and obesity classification using deep learning.

Materials and methods

In this retrospective, multi-institutional study, we analyzed 100,002 chest radiographs from 48,047 participants across three institutions. Images were uniformly quantized from the fixed 0-65535 range to 256 levels (0-255) with no additional processing. Three convolutional neural network architectures (ResNet52, EfficientNetB2, and ConvNeXtSmall) were trained on both 16-bit and 8-bit versions of the images. Model performance was evaluated using internal test datasets, randomly split multiple times, and an external test dataset. Statistical analysis included paired comparisons of area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC) values, with Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons.

Results

Across all architectures and classification tasks, differences between 16-bit and 8-bit model performance were minimal (mean differences ranging from -0.218%-0.184%). Statistical analyses revealed no significant differences in AUC-ROC values between bit depths for any model-task combination (all p values > 0.05 after Bonferroni correction). Effect sizes were small to moderate (Cohen's d ranging from -0.415-0.391).

Conclusion

No statistically significant differences were detected between models trained on 16-bit and 8-bit images in the three evaluated tasks. These findings suggest that conversion to 8-bit images may reduce data storage requirements and improve data processing efficiency. Further research is needed to assess their usefulness in clinical tasks.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence in Breast Cancer Diagnosis, Treatment, and Perioperative Management: A Systematic Review of Current Applications and Future Perspectives.

content.title: Artificial Intelligence in Breast Cancer Diagnosis, Treatment, and Perioperative Management: A Systematic Review of Current Applications and Future Perspectives.
content.abstract:
Background

Breast cancer is the most frequently diagnosed malignancy in women globally, accounting for approximately 2.30 million new cases and 666,103 deaths in 2022. Artificial intelligence technologies including machine learning, deep learning, radiomics, and natural language processing have been widely applied across the breast cancer care continuum. However, no systematic review restricted to primary studies with patient-level or image-level data has synthesized evidence spanning all clinical domains simultaneously.

Objectives

To evaluate the performance, methodological quality, and clinical relevance of artificial intelligence primary studies across screening and diagnostic imaging, digital pathology, radiomics, perioperative management, prognostic prediction, and natural language processing in breast cancer.

Methods

PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from January 2015 to May 2026. Eligibility was restricted to original primary research reporting patient-level or image-level data; secondary syntheses were explicitly excluded. Risk of bias was assessed using QUADAS-2 and PROBAST. Reporting followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines.

Results

Of 5,275 identified records, 17 primary studies met eligibility criteria. In screening mammography (seven studies; n = 7,540 to 144,231 examinations), deep learning achieved area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values of 0.876 to 0.939; a randomised trial in 80,033 women demonstrated non-inferiority to double reading with a 44.3% reduction in radiologist workload. In digital pathology (five studies; 270 to 44,732 whole-slide images), deep learning achieved AUC 0.985 to 0.994, exceeding unassisted pathologist performance in lymph node metastasis detection. Magnetic resonance imaging radiomics predicted pathological complete response in HER2-positive breast cancer with AUC 0.80. No breast cancer-specific perioperative primary study met the eligibility criteria. Deep survival networks achieved concordance index 0.626 versus 0.612 for Cox regression in breast cancer cohorts. Natural language processing identified metastatic recurrence in breast cancer clinical records with sensitivity 83% and specificity 73%. Risk of bias was low to moderate for imaging and pathology studies and high for small sample radiomics studies. Density-stratified performance was reported by only two imaging studies, and receptor status prediction from haematoxylin and eosin staining had not been validated as a safe alternative to immunohistochemistry.

Conclusions

Artificial intelligence demonstrated clinically meaningful performance across the five domains with eligible primary studies. Breast cancer-specific perioperative and intensive care primary studies were absent, representing the largest evidence gap. External validation, demographic diversity, and prospective clinical integration evidence remained the most consistently identified limitations. Prediction of molecular receptor status without immunohistochemistry requires rigorous prospective safety validation before it can complement standard testing.

records.title: Digital twin oncology and multi-omics-driven artificial intelligence models for personalized drug response prediction: A systematic survey of emerging computational paradigms and clinical implementation challenges.

content.title: Digital twin oncology and multi-omics-driven artificial intelligence models for personalized drug response prediction: A systematic survey of emerging computational paradigms and clinical implementation challenges.
content.abstract: The increasing complexity of tumor heterogeneity and variable therapeutic response has intensified the need for accurate personalized drug response prediction in oncology. Traditional trial-and-error chemotherapy strategies often result in suboptimal outcomes, toxicity, and delayed therapeutic adjustments. Rapid advances in multi-omics technologies, artificial intelligence (AI) and digital twin modeling have significantly reshaped computational oncology research. This survey systematically reviews peer-reviewed research and review articles published from 2021 onward that investigate emerging computational paradigms integrating digital twins and multi-omics AI for drug response prediction. The foundational concepts in digital twin oncology, multi-omics profiling and AI-driven precision medicine are outlined initially. The existing approaches are categorized into four major paradigms such as omics-driven machine learning models, deep learning based multimodal architectures, mechanistic digital twin simulation frameworks and hybrid digital twin AI systems enabling adaptive therapy optimization. The multi-omics data integration strategies, including early, intermediate, late, network-based and graph/pathway-based fusion techniques. The survey synthesizes recent developments in drug sensitivity prediction, immunotherapy response modeling, tumor evolution forecasting and virtual clinical trials, while critically analyzing challenges related to data heterogeneity, interpretability, generalization, privacy, regulatory compliance and ethical considerations. Finally, future directions are highlighted such as real-time adaptive digital twins, federated learning, explainable AI and regulatory ready clinical deployment frameworks. Overall, this review provides a structured taxonomy, comparative analysis and research roadmap for advancing integrated digital twin and multi omics AI systems toward clinically actionable precision oncology.

records.title: Is Large Language Model a New Hope for the Global South? A Rapid Bibliometric Synthesis of Artificial Intelligence in Anatomy Education.

content.title: Is Large Language Model a New Hope for the Global South? A Rapid Bibliometric Synthesis of Artificial Intelligence in Anatomy Education.
content.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), especially the recent proliferation of generative Large Language Models (LLMs), is transforming traditional anatomy education by introducing new teaching tools. However, the adoption of these cutting-edge technologies raises questions about global educational equity. It remains unclear whether AI will serve as a digital equalizer or further exacerbate marginalization. This rapid bibliometric synthesis aims to provide a comprehensive, data-driven overview of the "Application of Artificial Intelligence in Anatomy Education" (AAAE). We seek to map the intellectual landscape, detect structural and technological shifts, evaluate the geopolitical disparities, and provide corresponding references. A total of 85 consolidated records were retrieved from Web of Science and Scopus. These data constituted the whole panorama of AAAE. Bibliometrix and CiteSpace were utilized for static and dynamic mapping. A multidisciplinary expert panel validated the thematic clusters using Gwet's AC1 and the Normalized Herfindahl-Hirschman Index (HHI). Publications surged following ChatGPT's release, indicating a shift from specialized computer vision to the application of general-purpose LLMs. While high-income countries maintain leadership, AI could exert a "democratizing effect" on upper-middle-income countries, doubling their odds of publication compared to traditional anatomy. Six research frontiers and three research trajectories were captured, and corresponding implications for future researchers in the global south and north were presented. AAAE could be conducted using a stratified strategy: different expansions of AI technologies for pedagogy; leveraging commercial APIs to bypass infrastructure bottlenecks; and validating open-source models. Global equity critically demands cross-border collaboration and inclusive datasets.

records.title: From conventional imaging software to artificial intelligence: tools for stone volume assessment in urolithiasis. Α review by the EAU and YAU sections of endourology.

content.title: From conventional imaging software to artificial intelligence: tools for stone volume assessment in urolithiasis. Α review by the EAU and YAU sections of endourology.
content.abstract:
Introduction

Accurate assessment of stone burden is fundamental in urolithiasis, as it directly influences treatment selection and prognostic evaluation. Although maximum stone diameter on non-contrast computed tomography remains the most widely used parameter, it does not adequately reflect the three-dimensional complexity of urinary calculi. This review aimed to summarize the evolution of stone burden assessment from conventional imaging-based methods to software-assisted volumetry and artificial intelligence (AI)-driven tools, with emphasis on their accuracy, reproducibility, and clinical utility.

Methods

A narrative review of the literature was performed using PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Google Scholar for English-language studies published up to March 2026. Original studies, validation studies, technical reports, reviews, and guideline-related papers addressing conventional CT-based measurement, software-assisted volumetry, AI-based stone segmentation, and the clinical significance of stone volume were included. Due to heterogeneity in study design and reported outcomes, the evidence was synthesized narratively.

Results

Maximum stone diameter remains simple and widely available, but it incompletely represents true stone burden, particularly in larger or irregular stones. Formula-based ellipsoid calculations are practical yet show limited accuracy in complex geometries. Semi-automated CT-based segmentation software provides more reliable volumetric assessment, with excellent agreement with reference standards and reduced interobserver variability. AI-based approaches have further improved efficiency by enabling rapid and highly accurate automated stone detection and volume calculation. Across the reviewed literature, stone volume was consistently shown to be more clinically informative than linear dimensions for predicting spontaneous passage, stone-free rates after shockwave lithotripsy and ureteroscopy, and future symptomatic events during surveillance.

Conclusions

Stone volume offers a more accurate and clinically meaningful estimate of stone burden than maximum stone diameter alone. The transition from formula-based methods to software-assisted and AI-driven volumetry represents an important advance in urolithiasis imaging.
